Odesa Third Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Odes'ka oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. Odessa's Third Jewish Cemetery was established in 1905 and remains active today, with its newest tombstone dated as recently as 2018 — one of the more genuinely living cemeteries in this collection. According to the cemetery's keeper, its oldest preserved gravestones date to 1903, predating the cemetery's own founding by two years; these may have been relocated from one of Odessa's other, now-demolished Jewish cemeteries, documented elsewhere in this collection. With about 50,000 gravestones recorded, this is considered one of the largest Jewish cemeteries in Ukraine, serving the same enormous community that once numbered nearly 139,000 people by 1897 and endured the loss of over 40,000 in a single wave of massacres in October 1941.
